territorial_scope.description: Applies to autonomous vehicles operated on public roads in California.

evidence.quote: The autonomous vehicle is being operated on roads in this state solely by employees, contractors, or other persons designated by the manufacturer of the autonomous technology.

summary.short: Amends the California Vehicle Code so autonomous vehicles may not run on public roads until the DMV approves a manufacturer application; adds testing conditions, a $5 million insurance requirement, ADS marker lamp and lamp-color rules, and from 2030 a deployment permit for certain zero-emission vehicles.
summary.long: Sec. 1 amends Vehicle Code § 25950 on lamp and reflector colors, adding exceptions for ADS marker lamps on autonomous vehicles. Sec. 2 amends § 38750, defining autonomous technology, autonomous vehicle (SAE Level 3, 4 or 5), operator and manufacturer. It allows testing on public roads by a licensed driver when the vehicle is operated solely by employees, contractors or persons designated by the manufacturer, with a driver seated and a $5,000,000 insurance, surety bond or self-insurance requirement. Otherwise an autonomous vehicle may not operate on public roads until the DMV approves the manufacturer's application, which must include certifications on safety systems, data recording, federal motor vehicle safety standards, testing and insurance. The DMV must adopt implementing regulations and may impose additional requirements for vehicles without a driver; it must post public notice and wait 30 days before approving applications. Manufacturers must give purchasers a written disclosure of collected information. NHTSA federal rules supersede conflicting state provisions. From January 1, 2026, ADS marker lamps are permitted; from January 1, 2030, certain zero-emission autonomous vehicles of model year 2031 or later must operate under a deployment permit, with DMV rulemaking not before January 1, 2027.

"Autonomous technology" means technology that has the capability to drive a vehicle without the active physical control or monitoring by a human operator.
"Autonomous vehicle" means any vehicle equipped with autonomous technology that has been integrated into that vehicle that meets the definition of Level 3, Level 4, or Level 5

definitions.term: autonomous vehicle (exclusion of collision avoidance and driver-assistance systems)

evidence.quote: An autonomous vehicle does not include a vehicle that is equipped with one or more collision avoidance systems
"Department" means the Department of Motor Vehicles.
An "operator" of an autonomous vehicle is the person who is seated in the driver's seat, or, if there is no person in the driver's seat, causes the autonomous technology to engage.
A "manufacturer" of autonomous technology is the person, as defined in Section 470, that originally manufactures a vehicle and equips autonomous technology on the originally completed vehicle
For purposes of this subdivision, an "ADS marker lamp" means a device that emits a light to indicate when an ADS is engaged in the operation of the vehicle.
if the vehicle is a zero-emission vehicle, as defined in Section 44258 of the Health and Safety Code.

obligations.summary: Testing on public roads under subd. (b): the driver must be seated in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be able to take immediate manual control. Subd. (b)(1) limits operation to persons designated by the manufacturer.
obligations.conditional_on: Operation for testing under subdivision (b), if all requirements of (b) are met

evidence.quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver's seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle

obligations.summary: Before testing in California, the manufacturer performing the testing must obtain insurance, a surety bond or proof of self-insurance of $5,000,000 and provide evidence to the department. Subd. (c)(3) requires the manufacturer to maintain the same coverage in its application certification.
obligations.applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state

evidence.quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)

obligations.summary: An autonomous vehicle may not operate on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application that the department approves under subd. (d). The application must contain manufacturer certifications: (c)(1)(A)-(G) technical requirements (engage/disengage mechanism, cabin indicator, operator alert and takeover, FMVSS compliance, data capture), (c)(2) public-road testing, and (c)(3) insurance.

evidence.quote: Except as provided in subdivision (b), an autonomous vehicle shall not be operated on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application to the department

obligations.summary: Certified mechanism must capture and store autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, in read-only format, separate from other required mechanisms. Data must be preserved for three years after the collision.
obligations.conditional_on: Application under subdivision (c)(1)(G); the vehicle operating in autonomous mode

evidence.quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.

obligations.summary: The department must adopt regulations on evidence of insurance, the application and approval process, and notices of noncompliance. Regulations must include testing and performance standards. Under (d)(3) the department may adopt additional requirements, and under (d)(4) it must hold public hearings on regulations covering driverless operation.

evidence.quote: The department shall adopt regulations setting forth requirements for the submission of evidence of insurance

obligations.summary: The department must approve a manufacturer's application under subd. (c) if it finds the applicant has submitted all information and completed testing needed to show the vehicles are safe, and has complied with the regulations. Under (e)(2) the department may impose additional requirements for vehicles without a driver and may require a driver in the driver's seat.
obligations.conditional_on: Finding under subdivision (e)(1) that the applicant has submitted all information, completed testing and complied with the regulations

evidence.quote: The department shall approve an application submitted by a manufacturer pursuant to subdivision (c) if it finds

obligations.summary: When the department adopts the regulations under subd. (d), it must post a public notice on its website. It may not approve an application under those regulations until 30 days after the notice.
obligations.applies_from: 30 days after the public notice is provided
obligations.conditional_on: When the department adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d)

evidence.quote: The department shall post a public notice on its internet website when it adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d).

obligations.summary: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle must give the purchaser a written disclosure describing what information the autonomous technology collects.

evidence.quote: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology installed on a vehicle shall provide a written disclosure to the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle

obligations.summary: The department may adopt regulations to assess a fee on a manufacturer that applies under subd. (c), in an amount needed to recover its reasonably incurred costs.

evidence.quote: The department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee upon a manufacturer that submits an application pursuant to subdivision (c)

obligations.summary: From 2030, an autonomous vehicle of model year 2031 or later with a gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds may only be operated under a deployment permit under the California Code of Regulations, if it is a zero-emission vehicle. The text limits this to the extent authorized by federal law.
obligations.conditional_on: To the extent authorized by federal law; model year 2031 or later; gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds; zero-emission vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code 44258

enforcement.note: The amended text sets no fines, criminal penalties, or penalty maxima. Section 38750(d)(3) only empowers the department to adopt regulations with rules for revocation, suspension, or denial of licenses or approvals, without specifying any sanction, so no sanction regime is coded.
